paper_title: PyramidInfer Pyramid KV Cache Compression for High-throughput LLM   Inference
caption: The perplexity standard deviations when only PvCs are reserved at each layer.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates how the standard deviation of perplexity in log scale varies across model layers when only PvCs are reserved at each layer. The x-axis is labeled “Layer” and uses a linear scale, spanning from layer 0 to approximately layer 38, with major tick labels shown at 0, 10, 20, and 30. The y-axis is labeled “Perplexity (log) Std” on a linear scale, ranging from about 0.00 up to about 1.85, with regularly spaced tick labels at roughly 0.25 intervals (e.g., 0.00, 0.25, 0.50, …, 1.75). A single light-orange solid line with diamond markers is shown; it starts at a high value near 1.82 at layer 0, drops sharply to around 0.35 at layer 1, then decreases more gradually (around 0.31 at layer 2, ~0.27 at layer 3, and ~0.19 by about layer 4). From roughly layers 5–10 it stays in the mid–0.1 range (around ~0.16–0.18), then continues declining through the teens (around ~0.15 near layer 11 and ~0.09–0.10 around layers 13–14), reaching approximately ~0.03 by about layer 17 and around ~0.01 by about layer 20. From about layer 21 through the final layers, the markers lie very close to zero and remain nearly flat, ending near ~0.00 at the last layer.
